facts.fact: APS reports that the Taouey supercomputer, bought by the Senegalese state from Atos in December 2019, was officially put into service in March 2024 at the Cite du savoir in Diamniadio, and is described as increasingly needed for training AI models.
APS reports the 537.6-teraflop Taouey supercomputer is in service in Diamniadio, run by CINERI, with demand rising because of AI; the document does not name GPUs.

CINERI's director general Ousmane Thiare says Taouey has had more than a hundred users since its start, and that public and private users, including scientists of the sub-region, can use its high-performance computing services.

systems.platform: Atos, 537.6 teraflops, Cite du savoir Diamniadio
systems.owner: State of Senegal, administered by CINERI
